title: Remembering aunt only at the festival
odia:
ଦିନେ ନାଇଁ କାଳେ ନାଇଁ
ଗହ୍ମା ପୁନିଅଁକୁ ମାଇଁ ମାଇଁ।
literal_meaning: Not on any day, not at any time—but at Gahma full moon, “Aunt, aunt!”
meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟ ସମୟରେ ଖୋଜଖବର ନାହିଁ, ଗହ୍ମା ପୁନିଅଁ ଆସିଲେ ମାଇଁ ମାଇଁ ଡାକ—ଏହି ଅମେଳକୁ ଆମେ ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ। ନିୟମିତ ସମ୍ପର୍କ କିମ୍ବା ଯତ୍ନ ନରଖି କେବଳ ଏକ ଅବସରରେ ଆଗ୍ରହ ଦେଖାଇବାକୁ ଏହା ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରେ। କୌଣସି ଖାଦ୍ୟ କିମ୍ବା ଉପହାର ପାଇଁ ଡାକୁଛି ବୋଲି ମୂଳରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
explanation: Ordinary absence gives way to repeated affectionate address at a festival. We read this as criticism of attention that appears only for an occasion instead of being sustained. The verse leaves the reason for addressing the aunt unstated.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A group ignores a shared concern throughout the year but makes a great display of it on a special day. Someone recalls the aunt remembered only at Gahma full moon.
cultural_context: Gahma full moon provides a named occasion against the open-ended “not on any day, not at any time.” The repeated ମାଇଁ makes the sudden recognition audible; the verse does not explain any particular festival exchange.

witnesses.locator: Page24, eleventh item beginning ଦିନେ ନାଇଁ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload and comparison inspected17November2026; exact ଗହ୍ମା ପୁନିଅଁକୁ and ନାଇଁ retained. Usual absence versus occasional attention is contextual reading; no gift or ritual obligation inferred.
